title: Tech News with G. Dai — Episode 2
intro: Namaste! Welcome to episode two of Tech News with G. Dai. Five stories you need to know today. Let's get into it!

stories.headline: PHP2Shell flaw shuts Nepal's gov sites
stories.vo: Here's a wake-up call for Nepal! Two critical PHP flaws, called PHP-to-Shell, forced government and bank websites offline. PHP runs about seventy percent of the web, so patch early and upgrade old versions.

stories.headline: Nepalis put everyday AI to work

stat.label: bank-records task, done with AI help

stories.vo: Here's a surprise from Lalitpur! Ordinary Nepalis are using AI for real work. One bank employee wrote a script with AI that cut a three hour records check to one hour. Always verify the answers.

stories.headline: Google and NASA test a Moon-ready robot
stories.vo: Robots for the Moon are coming! Google and NASA tested an open-source AI model that moves a medical bag from plain English prompts. It succeeded eighty-five percent of the time in the lab, so it's early.

stories.headline: SK hynix profit hits a record
stories.vo: This is huge for chips! SK hynix just posted record quarterly results, with an operating margin of seventy-nine point seven percent. Its AI memory is sold out through twenty twenty-nine, so memory prices may stay high.

stories.headline: A hidden file can hijack coding agents

stat.label: success against Codex in a lab test

stories.vo: Coders, listen up! Researchers found a booby-trapped AGENTS dot M-D file can trick an AI coding agent into installing a rogue package. It worked ninety percent of the time on Codex in a test. Avoid running agents from Downloads.

outro: That's your tech brief for today. Follow G. Robotics for daily tech news, and I'll see you tomorrow!
